companies.name: Overland AI
companies.why: Off-road autonomy for military ground vehicles. Local and early, so equity still has room to grow.

companies.name: Anduril
companies.why: Autonomous defense hardware plus the software that ties it together. Has a Seattle office and an early-career track.

companies.name: Shield AI
companies.why: AI pilot software for drones and aircraft. Hires early-career engineers directly.

companies.name: Saronic
companies.why: Autonomous surface vessels for the Navy, scaling up its own shipbuilding.

companies.name: Helion
companies.why: Building a fusion power plant to sell electricity to Microsoft. A moonshot bet on cheap power for data centers.

companies.name: Zap Energy
companies.why: A smaller, simpler approach to fusion, built in the Seattle area.

companies.name: Crusoe
companies.why: Builds and runs AI data centers sited next to cheap energy.

companies.name: Baseten
companies.why: Runs other companies' AI models in production. Several roles list Seattle.

companies.name: Together AI
companies.why: GPU cloud and inference platform for open-source models.

companies.name: Modal
companies.why: Serverless GPUs, so developers run AI jobs without managing servers.

companies.name: Supabase
companies.why: Open-source Postgres backend that many new AI-built apps start on. Fully remote.

companies.name: Stripe
companies.why: Payments rails for the internet, now including AI companies. Large and stable but still private, with a real Seattle office.

companies.name: Figure
companies.why: Humanoid robots for factories and homes. A big, uncertain bet with huge upside if it works.

companies.name: Zipline
companies.why: Autonomous delivery drones already flying commercial routes. Real-world autonomy at scale.

companies.name: Relativity Space
companies.why: Building a reusable rocket to compete in the launch market. High risk, high upside.

companies.name: SpaceX
companies.why: Starlink is the cash machine: satellite internet sold to millions of homes, planes and ships, engineered in Redmond.

companies.name: Stoke Space
companies.why: Building a fully reusable rocket, plus Boltline, a software product other hardware companies pay for.

companies.name: Starfish Space
companies.why: Robot spacecraft that dock with satellites to refuel and extend them. Small team, early, local.

companies.name: Portal Space Systems
companies.why: Fast-moving spacecraft that can change orbits quickly, aimed at defense and space logistics. Very early.

companies.name: Blue Origin
companies.why: Big, well-funded rocket company in Kent. Its own careers site has no feed, so check it by hand.

companies.name: Echodyne
companies.why: Kirkland radar company whose sensors spot drones and protect borders and bases. Local and still private.

companies.name: Aurelian
companies.why: Seattle startup whose AI answers non-emergency calls so 911 dispatchers can focus on emergencies.

companies.name: Armada
companies.why: Portable data centers that bring computing to remote sites like oil fields and bases. Bellevue office.

companies.name: Collaborative Robotics
companies.why: Robots built to work next to people in hospitals and warehouses. Has a Seattle office.

companies.name: Lumotive
companies.why: Redmond chip startup that steers light with no moving parts, the eyes for robots and cars.

companies.name: K2 Space
companies.why: Builds very large, cheap satellites. Young and fast-growing, with Seattle roles.

companies.name: Docugami
companies.why: Kirkland startup whose AI reads business documents like contracts and turns them into data.

companies.name: Oleria Security
companies.why: Bellevue security startup that tracks who can get into what across a company's apps.

companies.name: Snowflake
companies.why: The data warehouse many AI teams feed their models from. Public and growing, with a big Bellevue office.

companies.name: Qumulo
companies.why: Seattle-born file storage for huge datasets, the unglamorous plumbing under AI and research.

companies.name: Stackline
companies.why: Seattle analytics company that helps brands sell on online marketplaces. Small enough to own real work.

companies.name: Truveta
companies.why: Bellevue company pooling health-system data for research. Past the risky early years, still private.

companies.name: Axon
companies.why: Body cameras, drones and the cloud software behind them. Large Seattle engineering hub that hires early-career.

companies.name: Aurora
companies.why: Self-driving trucks already hauling freight. Has a Seattle office.

companies.name: Whatnot
companies.why: Fast-growing live-shopping marketplace with Seattle-area engineering roles.

companies.name: OfferUp
companies.why: Bellevue's local buy-and-sell app. A mid-size team where one engineer touches a lot.

companies.name: Rover
companies.why: Seattle pet-care marketplace. Owned by private equity now, so less upside, but steady and local.

companies.name: Microsoft
companies.why: Runs Azure, the cloud much of the AI boom is built on. Home turf.

companies.name: NVIDIA
companies.why: Makes the chips nearly every AI company runs on. The purest picks-and-shovels company there is.

companies.name: Google
companies.why: Google Cloud and its own AI chips (TPUs). Large offices in Seattle and Kirkland.

companies.name: Meta
companies.why: Builds some of the largest AI data centers and infrastructure. Big Bellevue and Seattle presence.

companies.name: Databricks
companies.why: The data and AI platform big companies run on. Still private, so equity is still on the table. Has a Seattle office.

companies.name: Watchtower Labs
companies.why: AI and simulation software for military logistics planning. In-person Bellevue roles, U.S. citizenship required.

companies.name: Exia Labs
companies.why: AI wargaming and mission-planning software for the military, from an ex-Army officer and a Riot Games engineer.

companies.name: Worldscape.ai
companies.why: AI geospatial intelligence for defense, government and enterprise customers.

companies.name: EdgeRunner AI
companies.why: Offline, air-gapped AI agents for the military. Raised a Series A less than a year after its seed.

companies.name: Kapta Space
companies.why: Low-cost steerable radar sensors for satellites, from ex-Echodyne engineers. Likely hardware-heavy.

companies.name: ElastixAI
companies.why: AI inference infrastructure from ex-Apple engineers. Hires platform and Kubernetes engineers in Seattle.

companies.name: Edera
companies.why: Hardened container isolation for Kubernetes, AI workloads and GPUs.

companies.name: Tensor9
companies.why: Lets SaaS and AI vendors deploy inside customers' own secure environments. Founded by early AWS S3 engineers.

companies.name: Hyphen AI
companies.why: Generative AI that automates cloud app deployment.

companies.name: SageOx
companies.why: Tools for teams where humans and AI coding agents work side by side. Plans only a few key hires, so apply early.

companies.name: logcat.ai
companies.why: AI agents that debug device operating systems (Android and Linux in phones, cars, IoT).

companies.name: Devplan
companies.why: Coordinates product and engineering work around AI coding. Out of the AI2 Incubator.

companies.name: Ridge AI
companies.why: Embedded dashboards and data agents for SaaS apps, from Tableau and UW data-viz founders.

companies.name: Thira
companies.why: AI agents that handle IT tickets and back-office work, from the Apptio co-founders.

companies.name: Tektonic AI
companies.why: AI agents that automate complex business workflows.

companies.name: Pay-i
companies.why: Helps businesses track the cost and value of their AI use. Founded by Microsoft veterans.

companies.name: Aarden
companies.why: AI land intelligence for siting data centers and energy projects. Growing its technical team with fresh money.

companies.name: AZX
companies.why: Bespoke AI for utilities and energy companies. A public benefit corporation.

companies.name: Bayou Energy
companies.why: An API that pulls utility customer data for developers. Very small team.

companies.name: Clearly AI
companies.why: Reviews security and privacy risks before products ship.

companies.name: Staris
companies.why: AI 'virtual security engineers' for application security.

companies.name: StepSecurity
companies.why: Software supply-chain security for developers, from ex-Microsoft engineers.
